subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Space Robots: Exploring Without Humans
description: A micro-lesson that makes Space Robots: Exploring Without Humans usable.

hook.text: The Mars rovers drive themselves across an alien planet. A 20-minute signal delay makes real-time control impossible.

buildup.text: Curiosity and Perseverance use autonomous navigation. Onboard cameras and software plan paths around rocks without Earth input.

discovery.text: Each rover wheel is a separate motor. Six wheels with independent steering let the rover turn in place and climb rocks.

twist.text: The Canadarm on the ISS has seven joints and moves 100-ton modules in zero gravity. Precision in a vacuum, at 28,000 km/h.

climax.text: Ingenuity flew on Mars — the first powered flight on another planet. A robot helicopter scouting for a robot car.

punchline.text: Humans dream of Mars. Robots are already there.

quiz.question: Why must Mars rovers navigate autonomously?
options: The Martian atmosphere blocks radio signals from reaching the rover
A 20-minute signal delay makes real-time control from Earth impossible
The rover's computer is faster than any Earth-based control system
